title: Chapter 3 Quiz 1
description: The kinds of data a program handles, and the difference between a constant and a variable.
instructions: Take your time: read each question carefully, then check your answer.

questions.question: Which data type can hold only the values **True** and **False**?
questions.explanation: A Boolean holds one of two values: True or False.

questions.question: Which data type fits the value 2.15?
questions.explanation: Real numbers have a fractional part and are stored with a mantissa and an exponent. Watch out: 2.15 is not whole, so it cannot be an Integer.

questions.question: What is the data type of the value '7' written between quotes?
questions.explanation: Quotes make it a character (one byte matching an ASCII code), not a number. Watch out: it looks like a number, but quotes change its type.

questions.question: Match each value to its data type.
questions.explanation: Each value has a natural type: True is Boolean, -15 whole, 3.14 real, 'b' one character, 'COURSE' a string.

questions.question: A constant can be modified while the program is running.
questions.explanation: A constant keeps the same value for the whole program. Watch out: only a variable can change.

questions.question: What is a **String**?
questions.explanation: A string is a set of characters, for example 'COURSE'. A single character is one byte matching an ASCII code.

questions.question: A variable can hold which of these?
questions.explanation: The course lists three roles: input data, intermediate results and final results.

questions.question: An array is a set of data of the same type.
questions.explanation: An array groups values of one type, such as an array of integers.

questions.question: All data is encoded in {{1}} in the computer's memory.
questions.explanation: Everything in memory is encoded in bytes.
